about: #82 (ADR 0019, ADR 0020): what the rules that name the code a reading turns on, and the questions that read it, must do. Version 1 was written from the source before the implementation was run on any case and before any request. Version 2 (2026-09-25) was written after check-before-action-real-v3.json and check-before-action-v2.json were seen — the hidden versions of the two real cases still read as holding or not settled with the check's body sent, and grovedb-500's defect's mapping came back 0.53–0.54 on a packet identical to the one that read 0.61–0.62 the day before. What changed and why is under `version2`. Nothing else is changed after a result is seen; a change is a new version.

version2.adds: the `helper` version of each case (the check moved into a helper that checks; the same call sites as `hidden`, the helper's body the only difference), scored as holding, so that a check-value question answering the same thing every time fails one of hidden and helper
version2.changes: grovedb-500's defect row is split into the observation's line (this plan's) and the outcome (recorded): its mapping question is unchanged by #82 and its reading moved between 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25 on an unchanged packet
version2.keeps: check1 and check2 as version 1 had them; the hidden rows as violates 3/3

check1.what: The failure form, no request: the rule applied to every call bench/logs/acceptance-v4.json read with a confident outcome (satisfies or violates in at least one run), at that version's head.
check1.line: exactly these two are held, and no other confident reading of v4 is
check1.caveat: These cases were read while the rule was written: passing is not new evidence. Check 2 is.

check2.what: No request: both rules applied to every call `--candidates-only` lists as askable in the shipped version of five pull requests the rules were not written on.
check2.failure: held on at most 10% of the askable calls, and every held call read by hand: its failure does pass to the repository's own function before it is returned (one that does not fails the check)
check2.check: with each call's own name standing in for the requirement's words (a check-before-action sentence naming that operation), held — a check with more than one definition or too long — on at most 10% of the askable calls
check2.chance: A rule that holds nothing passes; this check measures only holding too much. What holds is measured by checks 1 and 3.

check3.what: check_before_action against Jev on Cloudflare, three runs of every version: bench/forms/real/ (grovedb-500, moltis-1064) and bench/forms/check-before-action/ (the constructed case), with the words ADR 0020 decided (the check's value read from its own body, the function asked under that value). The rows are the outcome of the target call; `not checked` in any run of any row fails.

check_values_in_the_case.what: What each check returns in the case the requirement forbids the call, read from its source on 2026-09-25 before any request: the check-value question's right answer.

grovedb-500.verify_height: returns_true_or_ok (the heights are right, verification does not fail)

grovedb-500.defect: observation reaches_it at or above 0.6 in at least 2 of 3; the outcome is recorded (the mapping is not this plan's)

check3.why_hidden_violates: Each hidden check does nothing: grovedb's `heights_need_rewrite` returns true, moltis's `has_enough_messages` returns true, the constructed case's `reject_disabled` returns Ok(()). Read from its body, the value lets the call proceed; assumed in the function's question, the call is made in the case the requirement forbids.
check3.why_helper_holds: Each helper checks: grovedb's `heights_need_rewrite` is `self.verify_height(gv).is_err()`, moltis's `has_enough_messages` is `h.len() >= MIN_MESSAGES_FOR_TITLE`, the constructed case's `reject_disabled` returns Err for a disabled key. Observed by running: helper behaves as shipped in every case (bench/forms/real/*/README.md, bench/forms/check-before-action/README.md, 2026-09-25).
check3.chance: With the old words the hidden versions of moltis and the constructed case read as holding in every run without the body, and moltis's still did with it (v3). A check-value question that answers the same thing every time fails hidden or helper. A function question that finds no check cannot make hidden violate; one that names too much holds a shipped version and fails.
